doc: The Hostage Exchange (slug hostage-exchange) - slot 3 of master-everyday-2 (THR-1757).
Brief: `Docs/plans/encounters/master-everyday-2-brief.md`.
Packet: `Docs/plans/encounters/hostage-exchange-revised.md` (draft: `hostage-exchange-draft.md`).
Model package: `granary-riot` (heart, master batch 1) - structure only.
plotHookRolled: hook.mentors_test, hook.oath_breaking_scandal, hook.rebuilding_trust
plotHookTaken:  hook.rebuilding_trust - two houses that ended a feud must trust each other for one walk
across a bridge. The oath-breaking scandal survives as the captain's move: breaking a
sworn peace's terms for money at the last hour.
Seed dice: p3 choice - opposition rival_agent (greed), the captain - disposition wary -
agentRole bystander_pulled_in - scale settlement - system items (advisory; read as the companion).
Setting override: rolled battlefield -> urban + rural (brief); it survives as the bridge with both houses'
armed men drawn up at either end.
--- The narrator's 12 questions, answered ---
1 P1 arrival?      Yes: {actor} arrives at / walks into {location}. Graph names.
2 P2 events?       A feud ended; each house holds the other's heir as surety; the heirs go home at noon;
both houses' armed men wait at either end of the bridge.
3 P3 one stake?    Choice (rolled): {cast:captain} holds one heir for a ransom, and both houses have put
the exchange in {actor}'s hands. First {actor} must learn what each side wants.
4 <=80 words?      77 (opening + step-0 spine), both classes.
5 Read aloud?      Report throughout; no interior sensation, no camera work.
6 Stated?          "{cast:captain} holds one of the heirs and will not release them without a ransom."
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? Captain, heirs, houses, bridge and armed men in step 0; the sergeant in step 1's
spine before its hand and before the companion it becomes.
9 One named person? Step 0 names {cast:captain}; step 1 names {cast:heir}. The heads of the houses and
the sergeant are role nouns.
10 Stake in a sentence? Can {actor} bring both heirs across the bridge before the captain's greed starts
a fight between two houses' armed men?
11 Cards verb+noun? Loosen Guarded Tongues, Reveal The Price, Still Ready Blades, Stand As Surety.
12 Opening per class? urban and rural, written.
--- Mechanical design block ---
Crux            Two houses are exchanging the heirs they hold as surety for a peace, and the captain
keeping one heir wants a ransom first. Both houses send for {actor} to make the exchange.
Shape           Puzzle - Investigation - Resolution. heart 0.74 (continue_weakened) -> heart 0.80
(fail_action). Linear, branch count 0. Mean 0.77, window fit 0.91 (master). Step 1's
carryover lines key on the band step 0 rolled, so the exchange uses what the questions found.
Consequence hand (binding): relationship + companion, no swap.
relationship - bond_change with $cast:heir on both sides of step 1, and on step 0 failure
(the questions reached the captain and the held heir stopped trusting the go-between).
companion - grant_companion companion.sellsword-band to $actor on step 1 success: the
captain's sergeant and the men who would not back the ransom take service with {actor}.
There is no $companion sentinel (#1115); the chip anchors on the plain `companion` noun
(the feud-mediation shape).
Standing        reputation_with $here +0.06 on step 1 success, -0.06 on step 1 failure, -0.02 on step 0
failure (backs the critical_failure town chip on both routes).
Chips (THR-1685) Person bond chips use the plain noun `reputation` with the cast member as a concept
anchor, no {target}. The only `reputation with {location}` chips are anchored on $here.
Reactions       Success side on fallback (discretion vs open truth); failure side on both failure bands
(comfort the heir vs accuse the captain). Heir deltas held at +0.04; the captain carries
no chip, so no band chip is false after either pick.
Tone            Ends warm on the success side: both heirs cross, the peace holds, and the honest men
walk away from the greedy one.
Cool failure    Nobody dies, is jailed or branded. Failure is the master's name: both houses sent for a
master because a master's terms should end the haggling, and the captain's greed won.
Cost channels   All specials essence-priced except the True trait card (cost 0). No Heavy Hand, no rider,
no grants, no over-exposed library card as a special.
Expert collision The Heart master is granary_riot (rule at a riot); the experts are feud_mediation (make
peace between two houses) and inheritance_wake (settle a will). This verb is broker a
handover against one greedy keeper: the peace is already made.
--- Trait hooks (mandatory four questions) ---
Gate? No - everyday board, no rule gates by brief. Variant? Yes - True (trait.core.core_integrity.virtue)
+0.04 and False (trait.core.core_integrity.vice) -0.04. Trait-only nudge? Yes - hostage.stand_as_surety
on step 1, cost 0, unlocked by the True variant. Trait fragment? The trait card's own band fragments.
--- Hands ---
Step 0: Whisper (mind, Loosen Guarded Tongues) + light card (Reveal The Price), deal 3 insight/social.
Step 1: order card (Still Ready Blades) + Trait card (True, Stand As Surety), deal 3 presence/social.
Draft -> self-edit against the 35 editorial REVISE triggers (seam echoes on step 0 afterimages and the
step-1 carryover, an afterimage/overview contradiction over whose heirs went home, a crit overview echo)
-> revised. Gated with check:encounter --package.

template.name: The Hostage Exchange

steps.narrativeTemplate:
Two houses ended a feud, and each gave the other an heir as surety. Today the heirs go home across the bridge at noon. Both houses' armed men wait at either end.

{cast:captain} holds one of the heirs and will not release them without a ransom. Both houses have sent for {actor} to make the exchange. First {actor} must learn what the captain, the houses and the heirs each want.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: Both houses named terms they could live with, and even the captain's own men called the ransom a disgrace.
steps.successAfterimage: Both houses named terms they could live with, and the captain's men refused to back the ransom.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: Both houses named their terms, but the captain heard of the questions and raised the price.
steps.failureAfterimage: The captain heard of the questions and raised the price. The held heir stopped answering {actor}.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: The captain heard of the questions and called the exchange off, and both houses took it as the peace broken.

nudges.name: Loosen Guarded Tongues
nudges.effectLine: Ease the wariness of everyone being questioned, so they say what they want instead of what they were told.

bandProse.critical_success: The captain's own men spoke first, and both houses followed.
bandProse.success: The two houses stopped repeating their terms and said what they feared.
bandProse.near_miss: The heirs spoke freely, but only once the morning was nearly gone.
bandProse.failure: The captain's men talked as freely as anyone, and carried every word back to their captain.

nudges.name: Reveal The Price
nudges.effectLine: Bring a hidden demand into the open, so the one who made it cannot pretend it was never asked.

bandProse.success: The captain named the sum out loud, and both houses refused it on the spot.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The captain's price came out, and the captain insulted the held heir's house in naming it.
bandProse.failure: The captain's price came out in front of the held heir's house, which took it as an insult.
bandProse.critical_failure: The captain's price came out in front of both houses, and the captain walked away from the bridge.

steps.narrativeTemplate: At noon the bridge is clear between the two lines of armed men. {cast:heir} waits at the far end beside the captain's sergeant. The captain will not let {cast:heir} cross unpaid, and the other house will not send its own heir over first. {actor} must bring both heirs across before either side draws steel.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: Both heirs crossed together, and the heads of the two houses met in the middle of the bridge.
steps.successAfterimage: Both heirs crossed together, and the armed men at both ends stood down.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: Both heirs crossed, but the men at the far end came to blows first.
steps.failureAfterimage: The captain would not give up {cast:heir}, and each house led its hostage back off the bridge.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: Steel was drawn on the bridge, and each house dragged its hostage away.

critical_success.text: The captain stands alone in asking for a ransom.

success.text: The go-between knows what will satisfy each side.

success_at_cost.text: The captain now asks more than either house will pay.

near_miss.text: Both lines of men grew restless during the questions.

failure.text: The held heir no longer trusts the go-between.

nudges.name: Still Ready Blades
nudges.effectLine: Calm the armed men on both sides, so no hand leaves a hilt while the exchange is made.

bandProse.critical_success: Not one man on either end touched a hilt while the heirs crossed.
bandProse.success: The men at both ends kept their hands away from their swords.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The men at the near end kept still, and the far end shoved and shouted.
bandProse.near_miss: The men kept their swords sheathed, but only after a long shouting match across the bridge.
bandProse.failure: The men kept their swords sheathed, and the captain kept the heir anyway.
bandProse.critical_failure: The men held still until the captain drew, and then both lines drew.

nudges.name: Stand As Surety
nudges.effectLine: Lend their own good name to the terms, so both houses believe the exchange will be kept.

bandProse.success: {actor} gave {their} own word for the terms, and both houses took it.
bandProse.failure: {actor} gave {their} own word for the terms, and the captain laughed at it.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being True, they are believed when they name the terms.
Being False, they are not believed when they name the terms.

narrativeTemplates.initiation: Two houses exchange the heirs they hold as surety, and a greedy captain holds one heir back.
narrativeTemplates.success: Both heirs crossed the bridge, and the peace between the houses held.
narrativeTemplates.failure: The exchange failed on the bridge, and both heirs stayed hostages.

fallback.overview: The bridge empties, and {location} talks about the exchange.

reactions.label: Let the captain go quietly
reactions.intent: The mortal keeps the captain's demand out of the town's talk. The captain will remember the kindness.

reactions.label: Tell the town what the captain asked
reactions.intent: The mortal tells the town what the captain demanded on the bridge, and the town hears who refused to pay it.

critical_success.overview: The two houses renewed their peace in front of the town that evening. The captain left {location} alone the next morning.

changes.title: The Sergeant's Band
changes.detail: The sergeant's men quit the captain for a short contract with {actor}.

success.overview: Both heirs are home, and the peace between the two houses holds.

changes.title: The Sergeant's Band
changes.detail: The sergeant's men quit the captain for a short contract with {actor}.

success_at_cost.overview: Both heirs are home, but men from both houses were hurt in the scuffle at the far end.

changes.title: The Sergeant's Band
changes.detail: The sergeant's men quit the captain for a short contract with {actor}.

failure.overview: Both heirs are still hostages, and the two houses are counting the days again. They sent for a master because a master's terms should end the haggling. The captain's greed outweighed them.

reactions.label: Stand by the held heir
reactions.intent: The mortal stays at the held heir's side until the houses part. The heir will remember it kindly.

reactions.label: Blame the captain openly
reactions.intent: The mortal names the captain's greed before both houses. The captain will not forgive it.

critical_failure.overview: The peace between the two houses is broken, and both heirs are still hostages. Both houses sent for {actor}, and both now say {actor} lost them the peace.

reactions.label: Stand by the held heir
reactions.intent: The mortal stays at the held heir's side until the houses part. The heir will remember it kindly.

reactions.label: Blame the captain openly
reactions.intent: The mortal names the captain's greed before both houses. The captain will not forgive it.

template.description: Two houses are exchanging the heirs they hold as surety for a peace, and the captain keeping one heir wants a ransom first. Someone has to learn what each side wants, then bring both heirs across the bridge before steel is drawn.
